text: The Patriots cruised past the Steelers 20-3 in their Week 2 home opener at Gillette Stadium, with the defense dominating in man coverage while TreVeyon Henderson punched in a touchdown run, though film study revealed mixed results from Drake Maye's performance in the contest. The victory marked a significant milestone—New England became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins—but the celebration was tempered by injury concerns, most notably starting right guard Mike Onwenu's broken right ankle that was confirmed by initial X-rays. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's lack of offensive rhythm compared to last season's Super Bowl run during his Monday press conference, highlighting that the defense will need to continue carrying the load while the offense continues developing consistency. The win demonstrated the team's ability to win ugly behind dominant defensive play, though questions persist about whether Maye and the offense can find the patient-yet-aggressive approach needed to complement what's clearly an elite defensive unit.
